Transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa (Redwood): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick check, does the time still work?
[00:12] Priya (Marigold - CISO): Yeah this is good, thanks. We wanted to focus the hour on governance things — SOC2 questions, where audit logs live, and the SSO run book.
[00:24] Marco (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll pull up the audit export slide i shared earlier. Just to set expectations, this is a short POC-check week, not an enterprise onboarding — we want to validate the hooks.
[00:36] Tom (Marigold): Yep that's correct. We're most worried about retention windows and whether we can pull logs into our SIEM without heavy parsing.
[00:44] Rita (Marigold): Also want to confirm who owns the timeline for SOC2 evidence — is Redwood providing evidentiary exports or we rely on instrumentation?
[00:56] Alyssa: Great question. High level, we'll provide the exports and the playbook for evidence generation, but responsibility matrix we'll map in the scoping doc. We'll note what Redwood can produce vs what Marigold has to instrument.
[01:10] Priya: Important that encryption key control is clear — if we use customer-managed keys, we need rotation logs surfaced.
[01:20] Marco: Right, we have KMS integrations. Quick caveat, in our hosted mode we support CMK via AWS-KMS and HSM for private. For the POC you're on hosted but we can demo the CMK flow. Expect some imprecise wording in the auto doc, but it does exist.
[01:35] Tom: Can you show where audit logs are kept? Are they tied to tokens or sessions?
[01:41] Marco: Logs are a mix — request metadata, model selection, and policy decisions. We store a structured audit trail; note that we do not keep full user input by default — that's on the retention config. For POC we can provide a full export.
[01:55] [Speaker 1]: (inaudible) snack --
[02:05] Priya: (laughs) ignore that, someone moved their mic.
[02:12] Marco: I'll share my screen — bear with me. So here's the audit export endpoint, it's a gzipped NDJSON output. Each line includes timestamp, model id, route, redacted prompt hash, and action. The sample includes an export script to push to S3 or pull into your SIEM.
[02:36] Alyssa: Note, sometimes the auto naming for our models shows up as "redwood-v1b" in the export; in your runbook we'll map to the human-friendly names you see in the console.
[02:48] Priya: For SOC2 we need tamper-evidence and immutable logs. Can you confirm write-once configuration or append-only exports?
[02:58] Marco: The export itself is immutable as generated, but storage immutability depends on where you place it. If you push to an S3 bucket with retention/lock, that achieves WORM. We can add a digest/checksum for each export to attest.
[03:12] Tom: How about retention policy enforcement? Can we set auto-delete after X days?
[03:18] Marco: Yes, retention is configurable per-tenant. For the pilot we can set short windows: 30/90/365 days. Important nuance — prompt-level data vs derived telemetry have separate retention controls.
[03:31] Priya: I'd like explicit mapping of which artifacts count as evidence for SOC2 CC6/CC7 — like session manifests, key rotation logs, access records.
[03:40] Alyssa: We'll add a responsibilities table in the scoping doc — that'll map artifacts to control IDs.
[03:46] Rita: Are there any known limitations in the POC environment vs Dedicated? For example, can we request near-real-time streaming of audit events?
[03:56] Marco: In hosted POC, export is near-real-time but some internal batching exists to save overhead. Dedicated offers lower latency exports and optional syslog push. I'll note that in the doc.
[04:08] [00:04:10] Priya: SSO — we want to do a test between our Okta sandbox and your SAML flow. What's the recommended pattern?
[04:18] Marco: We recommend IdP-initiated SSO for initial tests then SP-initiated for production. For the POC, we'll do an IdP-initiated test to validate assertion attributes (email, groups, role).
[04:30] Tom: We need group membership mapping to roles so our engineers get the right RBAC in Redwood.
[04:36] Alyssa: Marco will prepare a test checklist. Also, we support SCIM for provisioning if you want user autosync later, but not required for the POC.
[04:46] Marco: Quick note, some of the SAML attribute names that auto-transcribe get mangled — e.g., "urn:oid:2.5.4.x" shows as nonsense, we'll put the exact attribute list in the playbook.
[04:58] Priya: Encryption at rest — we want to confirm that embeddings and KV cache are encrypted under the same KMS policy.
[05:07] Marco: KV cache, embedding store, and object storage are encrypted; policy attachment can be configured per-tenant if you use CMK. For hosted without CMK, we still encrypt with provider-managed keys — so for SOC2 evidence you need the CMK flow.
[05:21] Rita: Anything in the backlog that might block our audit window? We have an internal milestone to collect evidence by Feb 10.
[05:28] Marco: No blockers on our side, just the SSO test and a short audit export validation. If we complete the two items, we can generate evidence bundle.
[05:35] Alyssa: Let's talk timeline quickly: Marco to send audit export example by 1/18, Alyssa to send SOC2 scoping doc by 1/20, SSO test on 1/22. That should give you enough to gather artifacts before Feb 10.
[05:48] [00:05:48] Priya: Sounds reasonable. A question — do you retain model prompts for debug, or are prompts redacted automatically?
[05:55] Marco: By default we redact PII and provide prompt hashes. For debugging we can enable a prompt-keep flag for the pilot but that'll be opt-in in the scoping doc and noted in retention.
[06:07] Tom: If we opt-in, how do we ensure only named engineers can retrieve raw prompts? Is there an audit trail?
[06:13] Marco: Yes, access to raw prompts is gated by RBAC and each retrieval is logged as an audit event. Those retrievals can be part of the SOC2 evidence set.
[06:26] Alyssa: Ok, any pushback or objections from the Marigold side?
[06:30] Priya: Just one: we want confirmation that any third-party subprocessors involved in logs handling (e.g., S3, cloud functions) meet our vendor risk threshold.
[06:40] Devlin (Redwood CSM): We maintain a vendor list and can provide a subprocessors matrix. We'll also include SOC2 status for those vendors where applicable.
[06:49] Rita: Great, please include that in the doc.
[06:53] Marco: Also small footnote — if you plan to simulate high QPS for performance, the audit export shape may change slightly; I'll include a note.
[07:02] [00:07:02] Priya: For retention, we may ask for a 90-day hot store and 7-year cold archive for specific artifacts. Is cold archive supported?
[07:12] Marco: Cold archive is supported via object storage lifecycle rules. We'll document how to configure immutability + long-term retention with S3 Glacier or equivalent.
[07:23] Tom: A quick logistics question — which AWS account will the exports land in during the pilot? Ours or Redwood's?
[07:29] Marco: We can do either. For security posture it's better to push to your account so you control lifecycle and access. For the POC we can demo both.
[07:36] Priya: Push to our account then — we'll supply a write-only role.
[07:40] Alyssa: Noted.
[07:42] Rita: Anything else on controls?
[07:44] Tom: I had a note about rate limiting and admin overrides — do admin actions appear in audit logs?
[07:50] Marco: Yes, admin actions are logged with actor identity and IP. Those are part of the evidence set.
[07:57] Priya: Good.
[08:01] Alyssa: Ok to recap real quick: 1) Marco sends audit export walkthrough + sample retention config by 1/18; 2) Alyssa sends SOC2 scoping and responsibility matrix by 1/20; 3) Schedule SSO test on 1/22 (Alyssa+Priya); 4) Tom to supply datasets list by 1/19; 5) Redwood to provide subprocessors matrix. Anything to add?
[08:27] Rita: Please also include the sample evidence bundle structure so our auditors can see the artifact layout.
[08:34] Marco: Will do. I'll attach a mock bundle.
[08:38] Priya: Thanks all, that addresses most concerns. We'll circle back after the SSO test and the export demo.
[08:45] Alyssa: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the docs and invites.

End of meeting.
